page.layout: One printed page. Running text in one column, with the page number and running head above it. A marginal note stands in the left margin beside the paragraph starting "Quintò Saul". The catchword "dere" stands at the right below the last line. The right edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: illasque perdit, Jud.15. v.4.5. Israël insidias ponit per circuitum contra Gibea, Jud.20. verf.29. Et quid pluribus opus est exemplis? Deus ipse pro populo suo stratagemate utitur contra exercitum Syrorum, audiri faciens ab ipsis strepitum, sonitum & tumultum castrense, quasi maximum hostium exercitum cervicibus suis imminentem haberent. Quo ceu Panico terrore in fugam convertuntur, 2.Reg.7. v.6.7. Ex quibus exemplis haec lex esto: In bellis justis, ad hostium vires, impressiones, & copias infringendas, stratagemata usurpantor. Nam, ut ille ait, dolus, an virtus, quis in hoste requirat? Pertinet huc, quòd Usia varias excogitavit & fecit machinas bellicas, quibus è turribus & muris Hierosolymorum lapides & tela in hostem conjiceret, 2. Paral. 26. A.15. Item quòd Ezechias, Sennaherib um[?] Hierosolymas obsessurum videns, fontium scaturigines extra urbem magno studio obturat atque tegit, ne aquari hostes possent, sed obsidionem citò solvere cogerentur, 2.Paral.32.v.3.4.

Vigiliæ bel-lorum tempore diligēter consti-tuendæ.Quintò Saul contra Philistæos bellum gerens, speculatores in Gibea Benjamin, in loco editiori collocat: qui ipsi nunciant, quòd multitudinem Philistinorum profterni & diffugere videant, 1.Sam.14.verf.16. David speculatorem habet, qui ei nunciat, filios ejus reverti incolumes, quos tamen omnes ab Amnone occisos fama retulerat, 2.Sam.13.v.34. page.notes: Printed page number 432 at top left; running head "LIBRI IV." centred and "De bellis." at right. "Usia" printed as is. "Sennaherib um" is doubtful: the printed word appears split, so it is marked [?]. The catchword "dere" stands alone at the right below the text. Left margin note is in the printed type of the margin, at the level of the second paragraph.
